lessons: Criterion 2 contradicts Scope-in. Scope-in has append() parse every line the instance has not cached, and it bans in-process shortcuts. So after k same-instance appends, the earlier appends have already parsed k-1 of the new lines, and the next read() parses 1 line, not k.

Amend criterion 2's same-instance case to: the next read() parses only lines this instance has not yet parsed, and exactly 1 when all k appends came from this instance after its last read. Keep 'exactly k' for appends by a second Journal on the same directory.

After the amendment, redo the full work from the merge base. Add the pure offset helper, cache rolled segments with a size check, and track the active segment's offset and line count. append() should read only the first line for the roll-age check and validate unseen lines before writing.

Review found sound: append() reuses the instance's single incremental cache to validate unseen lines before writing. Do not add a second append-only validation cache. It would re-parse bytes, which contradicts section 10's 'each byte once' sentence and is the dual path CLAUDE.md bans.
